name: Adani Total Gas Ltd
title: Adani Total Gas Ltd - 542066 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: CGD volumes strong (CNG +17%, PNG +5% in Q4) but gas cost pass-through is capped by consumer-first pricing; FY27 EBITDA guided loosely at ~INR1,500 crore vs FY26 INR1,225 crore.

summary.headline: Adani Total Gas Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% to INR1,696 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR310 crore; management guided FY27 EBITDA to about INR1,500 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,696 crore and EBITDA rose 13% to INR310 crore, with PAT up 4% to INR156 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 18% to INR6,415 crore, EBITDA rose 5% to INR1,225 crore, PBT fell 1% to INR863 crore and PAT was INR637 crore. Volumes carried the quarter: CNG grew 17% YoY in Q4 and PNG 5%, with a record ~50,000 domestic PNG connections added. Management said the West Asia crisis raised gas costs, which were partly absorbed to protect consumers, and that gas pool supply from the government was used to keep CNG and domestic PNG supplied.

financial_highlights.value: ~137,000 in FY26; ~50,000 domestic PNG in Q4 (highest ever)

segments.name: CNG (T)
segments.commentary: CNG volumes grew 17% YoY in Q4 and 18% in FY26. Network reached 705 stations after 25 added in the quarter, of which 140 are company-owned or dealer-owned dealer-operated.

segments.name: PNG (domestic)
segments.commentary: PNG volumes grew 5% YoY in Q4 and 6% in FY26. Total household tally reached 1.1 million (ATGL standalone) and 13.1 lakh including the IOAGPL JV.

segments.name: Industrial and commercial
segments.commentary: 214 customers added in Q4, taking the total to 9,965. Management said industrial volumes saw about 1% degrowth here and there during the crisis; industrial is about 20% and commercial about 2.5% of volume.

segments.name: E-mobility (ATEL)
segments.commentary: Operates 5,100 EV charge points across 26 states and UTs and 226 cities, with about 54 MW installed capacity. Target of 10,000 charge points in the near term.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to match FY26 growth, with possibly a little more from newer geographical areas (GAs).
FY27 EBITDA growth to track volume growth; management cited around INR1,500 crore of EBITDA for FY27.
Government targets natural gas at 15% of the energy mix by 2030; ATGL positions itself to support this.
capex_capacity: Steel pipeline network at 15,572 inch-km, plus over 8,300 km of MDPE pipeline.
Consolidated with IOAGPL JV: 1,169 CNG stations, 28,000 inch-km steel pipeline and 10,500 km MDPE.
ATGL serves 53 geographical areas: 34 directly and 19 through the IOAGPL JV.
Build pace cited: about 3 km of pipeline laid per day, one CNG station per week, 400+ home connections and 2 new businesses per day.
Nine city gas stations and one LCNG plant were connected in FY26 to bring new GAs onto mainstream gas; most of the 34 directly served GAs are now connected, with a couple pending.
demand_pricing: Gas pool price for March 2026 was USD 12.42 per MMBtu; the pool mixed domestic gas, withdrawn RLNG and fertiliser volumes, ONGC consumption, Vedanta and HPHT gas, and later contracted LNG.
Government circular of 9 March 2026 gave priority CNG and domestic PNG 100% of their six-month average gas, with extra volumes allocated later; GAIL acted as nodal agency.
Q4 CNG (T) gas sourcing: about 85% from APM allocation plus HPHT and WG volumes and other contracts; about 16% bought spot. Portfolio also includes Brent-linked and asset-linked contracts.
Q4 volume mix: CNG plus domestic PNG about 78%; industrial about 20% and commercial about 2.5% (balance of 22%).
Management said price was calibrated and not fully passed through to consumers to protect volumes, citing consumer-first approach.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gas pool price formula and which gases are in it (Dolat Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Pool price is the weighted average of pooled volumes: RLNG, fertiliser and ONGC volumes withdrawn, plus Vedanta and HPHT gas. March 2026 pool price was USD 12.42 per MMBtu; imported LNG was excluded in March but included later in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is supply sufficient for incremental CNG and PNG demand, and is spot LNG used (Dolat Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Government supplied the full six-month average, with additional volumes above it allocated later for the priority sector. Management did not give a split of spot versus government molecules for incremental demand.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue growth and EBITDA guidance (Mody Fincap)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Preyash Jhaveri guided revenue growth in line with FY26, with EBITDA growth tracking volume growth and cited around INR1,500 crore of EBITDA for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: When will new GAs reach peak utilisation and contribute to profit (Percept Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the 34 directly served GAs are now connected to city gas stations or LCNG plants. The initial focus is widening the consumer base, and it cited the highest-ever quarterly EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing flexibility to pass on higher gas costs (Percept Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices were calibrated and not fully passed on to protect consumers; industrial volume was down only about 1% here and there during the crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Returns on new investments and ROCE targets (Percept Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed target was given. Management said returns start lower in new GAs (around 8-10%) and rise to 12-15% with incremental investment on the same pipe, and it looks at 2-3 year and longer horizons.

qa_highlights.question: PNG volume split and Q4 sourcing mix (Emkay Global)?
qa_highlights.answer: PNG was about 50% of volume; CNG plus domestic about 78% and industrial plus commercial about 22%, with industrial about 20% and commercial about 2.5%. Sourcing mix: 85% APM, HPHT and WG plus contracts, 16% spot.

risks_watch: Gas cost pressure from West Asia tensions: spot and imported LNG cost more, and pool price effects on margins were not quantified.
Pass-through limits: management chose not to pass through full cost increases, which could pressure EBITDA margin if costs stay high.
Industrial and commercial demand softness and possible switching; industrial volume degrowth of about 1% was noted.
Sourcing dependence on government allocation (APM, pool) and whether priority allocation continues beyond the crisis period.
Returns on new GAs: ramp-up to 12-15% returns depends on incremental investment and consumer conversion from liquid fuels and LPG.
Interim CFO in place; continuity of financial reporting and guidance delivery to watch.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and customer additions, but defensive on pricing and returns: management repeatedly stressed consumer-first pricing and avoided giving sourcing split and return targets in numbers. The sourcing questions were answered only partially, and the spot LNG share for incremental demand was not disclosed.
key_quotes: Customer addition remained strong with nearly 50,000 new domestic PNG connections added in this quarter, which is our highest addition ever.

So as I always say, for us, consumer is the first, which we do because wider the consumer base, profitability will be kept happening better and better rather than continue suddenly start passing on everything on the consumer, whether he can afford or not, and we'll see dropping of our consumer base.

Every day, we are connecting 400 -plus home connections. Every day, we are connecting 2 new businesses. Every week, we are building 1 CNG station. Every day, we are laying 3-kilometer pipeline in the country.

adds.what: Nine city gas stations and one LCNG plant connected in FY26 to bring new GAs onto mainstream gas (already done, not new capacity)
25 CNG stations added in Q4 FY26, taking network to 705 stations

growth.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth to match FY26's ~18% (plus a little from new GAs) and FY27 EBITDA of about INR1,500 crore (vs INR1,225 crore in FY26), backed by ongoing CNG station and PNG connection build-out (about one CNG station per week, 400+ home connections per day) and a 1,169-station consolidated network, though no order-book or capex amounts were quantified.
